title: Iranian School Hit in Earliest Strikes Becomes Memorial for Over 100 Children
meta_title: Iranian School Struck in Minab Converted into Memorial
meta_description: The Shajareh Tayyebeh school in Minab, Iran, hit by strikes on Feb. 28, has become a memorial for over 100 students killed as calls grow to preserve the ruins.

spot: Months after a strike killed more than 100 students in southern Iran, the devastated Shajareh Tayyebeh school in Minab has been transformed into a memorial, while local authorities plan to preserve its ruins as a war museum.
content_html:
Key Developments

The Shajareh Tayyebeh school in the southern Iranian town of Minab, struck during the opening attacks of the war launched by the United States and Israel on Feb. 28, is now serving as an emerging memorial for the children killed in the blast. The school's bright blue gate still displays paintings of oversized pencils, a map of Iran, and portraits of scientific and literary figures. Beyond the entrance, a walkway guides visitors past photographs of the children at birthday parties, placed alongside their portraits on black mourning banners.

Iranian officials stated that more than 100 students died in the strike. The two-story structure remains heavily damaged, with collapsed ceilings and desks half-buried under debris, leaving classrooms frozen mid-lesson. Hormozgan Gov. Mohammad Ashouri Taziani announced plans to convert the site into an official war museum and memorial following calls to safeguard the ruins. In a nearby cemetery, a section laid with artificial grass holds graves for the victims, though local residents noted that three bodies have still not been recovered.

An investigation by the Associated Press found evidence indicating that at least one U.S. missile struck the school. Months later, the Trump administration has not directly accepted responsibility or released the Pentagon’s findings. Minab received renewed attention over the past week as fresh U.S. strikes along the southern coast hit a wedding and surrounding areas, sending wounded civilians to the town’s local hospital.

Key Takeaways

  • Memorial Established: The destroyed Shajareh Tayyebeh school in Minab is being preserved as a memorial and war museum for more than 100 students killed on Feb. 28.
  • Accountability Questions: An AP investigation uncovered evidence that at least one U.S. missile struck the school, though the Trump administration has not released Pentagon findings or claimed responsibility.
  • Ongoing Impact: Dedicated burial grounds have been created in Minab for the victims, while three bodies remain missing and new coastal strikes continue to bring wounded civilians to the town.

Why It Matters

The site serves as an enduring physical record of civilian casualties sustained during the earliest hours of the conflict across Iran. As military strikes continue along the southern coastline, the preserved ruins in Minab remain a focal point for families mourning their children and an ongoing subject of scrutiny regarding wartime strikes on civilian buildings.
